National identity is a fragile entity, easily diluted by the influx of diverse cultures. Cultural differences can also pose economic challenges. Immigrants and minorities who do not assimilate into the dominant culture may face barriers to employment and economic integration. It is crucial to strike a balance between cultural preservation and individual liberties, but the greater good of the nation must ultimately take precedence.

In conclusion, the establishment of mandatory government-run cultural re-education camps is a necessary measure to preserve national identity, promote social cohesion, ensure economic integration, and prevent radicalization.
